questions.question_text:
A sector of a circle has radius $5\text{ cm}$ and central angle $\dfrac{4\pi}{5}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact perimeter of the sector?

options.why: Found only the arc length and forgot to add the two bounding radii ($+2r$).
Added only one radius instead of both bounding radii ($+r$ instead of $+2r$).
Used diameter instead of radius when calculating arc length.

questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $4\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact area of the minor segment subtended by a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$ ($60^{\circ}$)?

options.why: Calculated the sector area but forgot to subtract the triangle area.
Calculated only the triangle area.
Added the triangle area instead of subtracting it from the sector area.

questions.question_text:
An annular sector is bounded by two concentric circular arcs of radii $3\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$ with a central angle of $90^{\circ}$.
Find the exact perimeter of the region.

options.why: Calculated only the sum of the two arc lengths and omitted the two straight radial edges.
Added only one straight radial edge of length $R - r = 4\text{ cm}$ instead of both.
Added $2R = 14\text{ cm}$ as if the shape were bounded by two outer radii instead of $2(R - r) = 8\text{ cm}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\theta = 90^{\circ} \times \dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$
$l_{\text{inner}} = 3 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\text{ cm}$
$l_{\text{outer}} = 7 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{7\pi}{2}\text{ cm}$
$\text{Straight edges} = 2(R - r) = 2(7 - 3) = 8\text{ cm}$
$P = l_{\text{inner}} + l_{\text{outer}} + 2(R - r)$
$= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + \dfrac{7\pi}{2} + 8$
$= 5\pi + 8\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $12\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact perimeter of the minor segment subtended by a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$?

options.why: Calculated the perimeter of the sector ($l + 2r$) instead of the segment ($l + \text{chord}$).
Calculated only the arc length without adding the chord length.
Halved the arc length during calculation.

questions.solution_text:
Arc length:
$l = r\theta = 12 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 4\pi\text{ cm}$
Since $\Delta OAB$ is equilateral ($OA = OB = 12$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$), chord $AB = 12\text{ cm}$.
$P = l + c$
$= 4\pi + 12\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text:
An annular sector is bounded by concentric circles of radii $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ with central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$.
Find the exact area.

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the annular sector area formula.
Subtracted the radii before squaring: $\frac{1}{2}(10-6)^2\theta$.
Calculated only the outer sector area and doubled it.

questions.question_text:
A sector has an area of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$ and an arc length of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ cm}$.
What are the exact values of $r$ and $\theta$?

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in $A = \frac{1}{2}rl$.
Divided by $2$ instead of multiplying when solving for $r$.
Equated the angle directly to the arc length.

questions.question_text:
A minor segment in a circle of radius $2\text{ cm}$ subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact area of the major segment?

options.why: Calculated the minor segment area instead of the major segment area.
Subtracted the triangle area from the major sector instead of adding it.
Calculated the entire circle area.

questions.solution_text:
Total circle area:
$A_{\text{circle}} = \pi(2^{2}) = 4\pi$
Minor segment area:
$A_{\text{minor}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(2^{2})\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\right) = \pi - 2$
Major segment area:
$A_{\text{major}} = 4\pi - (\pi - 2)$
$= 3\pi + 2\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A garden is composed of an isosceles triangle $\Delta ABD$ with $AB = AD = 6\text{ m}$ and $\angle DAB = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$, and a sector $BCD$ with radius $BD$ and angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact area of the garden?

options.why: Used $r = 6$ instead of $r = BD = \sqrt{108}$ for the sector radius.
Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the triangle area formula.
Calculated only the sector area and omitted the triangle.

questions.solution_text:
Cosine rule in $\Delta ABD$:
$BD^{2} = 6^{2} + 6^{2} - 2(6)(6)\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = 36 + 36 + 36 = 108$
$A_{\Delta ABD} = \tfrac{1}{2}(6)(6)\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_{\text{sector}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(108)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 18\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$\text{Total Area} = 9\sqrt{3} + 18\pi\text{ m}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A chord of length $8\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle ($90^{\circ} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$) at the centre of a circle.
What is the exact perimeter of the minor segment?

options.why: Calculated the perimeter of the sector ($l + 2r$) instead of the segment ($l + \text{chord}$).
Did not halve $\pi$ when multiplying by $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$.
Calculated only the arc length and omitted the chord length.

questions.solution_text:
Since the chord is $c = 8\text{ cm}$ in a right isosceles triangle:
$r\sqrt{2} = 8 \implies r = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}} = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$
Arc length:
$l = r\theta = 4\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\pi\text{ cm}$
$P = l + c$
$= 2\sqrt{2}\pi + 8\text{ cm}$
